quizzes.question: Containing an estimated 390 billion individual trees across 16,000 distinct species, this biome plays a vital global role in carbon sequestration. Ongoing deforestation driven primarily by cattle ranching and agriculture severely threatens its ecosystem across nine South American nations, over sixty percent of which lies in Brazil. For the point, name this largest tropical rainforest in the world.
quizzes.explanation: The Amazon Rainforest is the world's largest tropical rainforest, containing about 390 billion trees and spanning nine South American countries, with over 60% located in Brazil.

quizzes.question: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal form of this quantity points toward the center of curvature with a magnitude of velocity squared divided by radius. For the point, name this rate of change of velocity over time, measured in meters per second squared.
quizzes.explanation: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity over time and is governed by Newton's Second Law (F = ma), with standard SI units of m/s².

quizzes.question: Nevado Mismi in the Peruvian Andes has historically been identified as the ultimate headstream of this massive river system. quizzes.explanation: The Amazon River originates in the Peruvian Andes and releases more water volume than any other river system, contributing around 20% of global ocean river discharge.

quizzes.question: The LIGO experiment directly detected ripples in spacetime caused by this fundamental interaction in 2015, confirming a major prediction of general relativity. quizzes.explanation: Gravity is the fundamental force causing mutual attraction between objects with mass, classically formulated by Newton and reinterpreted by Einstein's general relativity.
